fieldValues.title: The three trigram lines are the foundational axes
fieldValues.decision_question: What are the axes against which every domain, tension, decision and stance in our work is placed?
fieldValues.context: The three lines are already used in many places: the handbook chapter 'A domain's axes' (proposed, not in force), the decision-taxonomy exercise (two blind raters per line agreed at kappa 0.90, 0.84 and 0.81 on 101 decisions), the eight stance archetypes, the domain axes (axis-in-domain), the fractal map of the archetypal flow, and the older products model (orientation, change dynamics, perspective). The owner, 2026-10-25: 'These are the three trigram lines. They are used all over our work. And should be foundational.' The owner, 2026-10-28 (vignette 66658bf5): the base trigram axes and poles apply by default and any decision can be mapped against them, giving each decision a trigram; the trigrams show our basic stance; the maps are never absolute, always relative to a domain, and judgement is refined by the other decisions within it; consistency over time builds a consistent system, as the compass shows cell by cell. The base poles are already affirmed on the base domain Semantic engineering in practice (Act/Observe, Disrupt/Stabilise, Focus/Zoom out). This record stayed in draft from 2026-10-25 with status proposed, so it never reached a session (finding, 2026-10-28).
fieldValues.friction: Each use states the lines in its own words and none is in force, so a new domain, decision or stance can be placed on different axes from the last.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
1. Do nothing: each practice keeps its own statement of the lines. Leads to: drift between the stance, domain and decision uses.
2. The three trigram lines are foundational, stated once, and every other use points to them (recommended). Leads to: one frame to place and compare domains, tensions, decisions and stances; narrower domains may flip a line's polarity (cdd272a3).
3. Use the twelve-cell compass as the foundation instead. Leads to: a fixed grid that finds gaps well but is harder to recognise in practice; it stays as the map for finding gaps.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Understeer: uses keep their own wording, and placements cannot be compared across domains. Oversteer: every trade-off is forced onto a line where it does not fit (the first fractal map tried three per stage and two failed the definition of a trade-off), or the lines are treated as truth rather than a lens.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Every domain, tension, decision and stance is placed on three trigram lines, stated once: line 1, act now and outward, or gather information and refine ourselves (Act ↔ Observe); line 2, disrupt by evolving and adding new things, or stabilise by simplifying and refining what is present (Disrupt ↔ Stabilise); line 3, the scale of the boundary, small and closed with a few mostly internal options, or open with many options, many of them external (Focus ↔ Zoom out). The lines apply by default in every domain, relative to that domain: renamed and refined there, never absolute. A decision's placement on the three lines is its trigram; the trigrams of a domain's decisions show its stance, and judgement on a new decision is refined by the earlier decisions in the same domain, so that consistency over time builds a consistent system.
fieldValues.rationale: Good enough for now: the lines already recur across the work, raters agree on them, and the owner names them as foundational. Every decision is an experiment, so this one is too.
fieldValues.revisit_when: A domain's trade-offs repeatedly fail to place on any line, or raters stop agreeing on a line's reading, or a fourth axis keeps appearing (the older products model allowed a domain-specific wildcard).
